reading.body:
Amazon IAD65 is an individual building within AWS's Northern Virginia data center campus, which spans Loudoun, Prince William, and Fairfax counties. AWS does not publish power capacity, floor area, or technical specifications for individual facilities as a matter of stated security policy, so the critical IT load and rack count of this building cannot be independently verified. The campus sits in an area known as Data Center Alley, reported to host the world's largest concentration of data centers.

AWS committed $51.9 billion to Virginia infrastructure between 2011 and 2021 and announced an additional $35 billion investment through 2040. Approximately 70% of global internet traffic reportedly moves through Virginia data centers. These figures establish the regional significance of the Northern Virginia cluster, though individual building capacity remains unpublished. Virginia has 326 mapped data center facilities, of which only 23 operators have published power specifications totaling 1,375 megawatts.

This building cannot be ranked among published capacity in Virginia because AWS does not disclose its specifications. The absence of a published figure does not indicate the facility is small or incomplete; rather, it reflects AWS's standard disclosure practice across its global footprint. Assessing whether this campus matters to AI scaling requires relying on regional aggregates and AWS's stated capital commitments rather than facility-level data.
